messages:
maya: Heads-up — seeing sporadic OOM spikes on multi-turn runs (seq 2048+) after the recent kernel-chooser tweak. Memory accounting shows the workspace estimate inflates ~2x *before* kernel pick. Suspect FlashAttention estimate or pad-to-align logic is blowing up.

sam: Which change are you referring to? the chooser PR (4128) that prefers cuBLASLt for certain batch/hidden combos? can you paste profiler output or a pmap?

maya: Yep PR#4128. Quick profiler dump (local repro):

```
# sample gmem snap
PID 2191 GPU0 MemUsed 23900MiB
workspace_estimate: 5.2GB -> 11.1GB  # jumps right after chooser decision
kernel_chosen: cuBLASLt_ffn_fallback
kernel_budget: 9.6GB  required: 10.9GB
tracepoint: pad_align=256, batch=6, seq=2048, head_dim=128
```

leo: That lines up with cuBLASLt fallback behavior — when pad_align=256 we end up with big temporaries for the fallback path. Also some cuBLASLt algorithms ask for extra scratch that we don't account for in the fast path. Did we flip any pad or alignment flags in the heuristic config?

maya: We turned on align256 heuristically for batch>=4 to get better throughput on smaller heads. Turns out that triggers the fallback and the workspace reservation balloons. Also noticed KV cache reuse isn't fully reclaimed between segments in this repro, so slab pressure doubles.

zara: Short term mitigation: can we pin the chooser to prefer Triton-FFN for seq>1024 or for cases where pad_align=256 would be required? Rollout to 5% canary and watch OOM rate.

sam: Add a probe first: set DEBUG_WS=1 on canary and run microbench to capture pre/post kernel workspace sizes. Also run `alloc_trace.py --trace-workspace` (commit 9b3f2a) and upload the tarball to the thread.

jon: Idea for medium-term: allow transient borrowing of FFN scratch buffers from KV cache slab when page/align compatible. Mark borrowed pages read-only for KV until reclaimed asynchronously — should avoid synchronous fallback allocations. Low-risk if opt-in.

maya: Jon — that looks promising. For immediate hotfix I reduced workspace-reserve-fraction from 0.25 -> 0.15 on hosts with >64GB and it prevented OOMs in my local loop. Not ideal long-term but buys time.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout started: kernel-chooser pin to Triton-FFN at canary 5% (deploy id d-20260318-77).

zara: :thumbsup: After canary is up, collect telemetry keyed by kernel, device, seq_len, batch, and KB/MB of workspace. If OOMs drop, promote.

sam: Also add a cuBLASLt safety padding: some algos underreport workspace. Suggest safety_padding = max(0.05 * est, 32MB) before making final reserve. That should absorb underestimates without massive over-reservation.

maya: I'll open an RFC with the changes: 1) temporary chooser pin to favor Triton for affected shapes, 2) reduce default reserve fraction for high-memory hosts, 3) add cuBLASLt safety padding, 4) opt-in KV-borrowing for scratch reuse. Assigning to myself to run prod microbench and collect traces. attaching short trace excerpt:

```
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] trace ws_pre: 5200000000
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] chooser decision -> cuBLASLt_ffn_fallback
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] ws_post: 11100000000  # 2.13x
[2026-03-18T14:03:26Z] alloc_fail OOM candidate slab=kv_cache id=7
```

maya: Will attach alloc_trace tarball and perf counters once the canary run completes. Thanks all for quick triage.
